Title: Trump threatens to annihilate Iran as diplomats push for deal at UN
Article:
UNITED NATIONS: US President Donald Trump warned on Tuesday that he could annihilate Iran if there is no deal to end the war, but also suggested an agreement could come soon amid a diplomatic push at the United Nations.
"I have a big decision to make," Trump said in a speech at the UN General Assembly in New York.
"Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before?.. Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?"
In a statement on Tuesday, Iran's Armed Forces dismissed Trump's comments at the UN as "propaganda", saying their response is "full readiness to inflict more severe, crushing, and unpredictable blows on the aggressors."
But away from the fiery rhetoric, discussions continued to try to end the nearly seven-month conflict that began with joint US-Israeli strikes and has since killed thousands, driven up oil prices and drawn in neighbouring countries.
Trump said that envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner "had a very productive meeting today with mediators of Iran."
"I think there's a lot of momentum for them to make a deal," he said.
Trump also met the leaders of Middle Eastern countries who are keen to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, the conduit for a fifth of global oil and gas shipments before the war, but are wary of giving their longstanding rival Iran too much power.
Many also host huge US military bases that have come under repeated Iranian attack throughout the war.
"We think that the situation with Iran could end right after the (Nov 3) midterm elections, maybe before. I don't know. You never know," Trump said as he met the leaders.
The diplomatic manoeuvring comes as Trump faces pressure on multiple fronts — rising energy costs at home, a widening regional conflict abroad, and the midterms six weeks away that could reshape his political standing.
Whether talks produce a deal or the war escalates further carries consequences for global oil markets, Gulf security and millions of Iranians.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi met with Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani of Qatar, which has spent months trying to de-escalate the conflict, the Qatari state news agency reported.
A senior Iranian official said Teheran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within days if the US eased military pressure and lifted its blockade on Iranian ports.
The senior Iranian official told Reuters that Teheran had conveyed its latest proposal to Washington through mediators last week and could reopen the strait to Gulf shipping within seven days if its demands were met.
In a reminder of Iran's firm position so far, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, who headed Iran's negotiating team at previous talks, said Iran would never surrender: "Trump must understand that he cannot impose his power on the Iranian people and its armed forces."
Widening regional conflict
On the table at the Gulf states' meeting with Trump is a Qatari proposal for a common security framework involving Iran and the Arab Gulf states, regional sources said. One source said Iran was reviewing the proposal.
Al Thani has said any such arrangement would need to provide security guarantees for the Gulf states and expand economic interdependence with Iran.
Saudi Arabia, the largest of the Gulf states, has been drawn deeper into the war this month as Iran-aligned Houthi fighters have advanced in Yemen, routing forces of the Saudi-backed government and threatening Saudi oil exports through the Red Sea.
The US, which bombed the Houthis for two months last year, has so far rebuffed repeated pleas from Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to rejoin the fight. The New York Times reported that Trump called off US strikes against the Houthis on Sunday at the last minute.
Asked why Washington had held back from striking the Houthis, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the United States would always support Saudi Arabia, adding:
"That said, that is a very dangerous and complex conflict that pre-exists ... We have a history with the Houthis as well, and that's something we don't want to see impacted either."
Oil markets did find some relief on Tuesday after sources told Reuters that Saudi Arabia had restarted operations at its East-West Pipeline and could resume exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu within hours, albeit at reduced volumes.
The pipeline, Saudi Arabia's main export route bypassing wartime disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, had been shut after attacks this month that Riyadh blamed on Iranian-backed groups in Iraq.

Title: Israel denounces 'grotesque absurdity' of Macron UN remarks on West Bank
Article:
JERUSALEM: Israel shot back angrily Tuesday at French President Emmanuel Macron, who criticised Israeli actions in the West Bank by saying Hamas was not active in the territory that is home to the Palestinian Authority.
"The grotesque absurdity of Emmanuel Macron's statement is staggering," said a statement by the office of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is expected to deliver a defiant address to the world body on Thursday.
"Hamas terrorists carry out attacks against Jews almost every day. They have murdered countless Israeli civilians in Judea and Samaria," it said, using the Biblical name for the West Bank, which Israel seized in 1967.
Netanyahu's office pointed to the shooting death on Sunday, on the eve of Judaism's holiest day of Yom Kippur, of an Israeli settler in the West Bank. Israel said that the victim, father of six Netanel Shukrun, also had French citizenship.
The Israeli military said it arrested the Palestinian gunman at a hospital and troops later raided his village. A minister in Netanyahu's government called for his execution under a new law.
Extremist Israeli settlers frequently attack and steal from West Bank Palestinians. The United Nations said there were about six settler-related violent incidents against Palestinians or their property daily through mid-2026 in the territory.
Macron in his speech to the United Nations deplored the humanitarian situation in Gaza — from which Hamas led the Oct 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest ever against Israel — as well as actions by Israel in the West Bank.
"What is our credibility worth if we remain inactive on Gaza? Some claim that peace has been achieved, but this has not opened up humanitarian deliveries. It is a spectacle that shames us all," Macron said.
"Look at what is happening in West Bank, where there are violations every day. In the name of what? Hamas has never struck in the West Bank. This every day makes it more impossible to achieve respect for the Palestinian people's legitimate right to exist."
The Palestinian Authority, led by Hamas's rivals, has semi-autonomy in major urban areas of the West Bank, with Israel controlling most of the territory.
Hamas took over Gaza in 2007, two years after Israel pulled out and dismantled settlements.
Netanyahu has poor relations with Macron, who led a push by Western nations at last year's UN General Assembly to recognise a Palestinian state.
France recently joined Britain in imposing sanctions on products from Israeli settlements in the West Bank, again angering the Israeli government.

Title: Rapid KL deploys alternative trains after Putrajaya Line brake system malfunction at Jalan Ipoh Station
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — A brake system malfunction on a train at Jalan Ipoh Station caused a disruption on the Putrajaya Line today, Rapid KL said.
The operator announced the incident in a media statement issued this morning.
Rapid KL said it activated alternative train services to maintain passenger movement along affected stretches of the line.
“Technical teams have been dispatched to inspect and repair the affected system,” the operator said.
Rapid KL added that police officers and station staff had been deployed to assist passengers during the disruption.
Rapid KL listed the following alternative train arrangements:
Trains from Kwasa Damansara Station turning back at Jalan Ipoh Station — five‑minute intervals
Trains from Hospital Kuala Lumpur Station turning back at Putrajaya Sentral Station — six‑minute intervals

Title: Haze worsens: Two Sarawak areas hit ‘very unhealthy’ API levels, Kanowit at 244, Lubok Antu at 205
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 23 — Kanowit and Lubok Antu recorded very unhealthy air pollutant index (API) readings this morning, with the former registering the highest reading in Sarawak at 244.
According to the Natural Resources and Environment Board (NREB) API Status for Sarawak, the two stations were the only locations in the state recording API readings in the ‘Very Unhealthy’ category as of 8am.
Lubok Antu recorded an API reading of 205.
All other areas, except Bario, recorded API readings in the ‘Unhealthy’ category.
Sri Aman recorded the highest ‘Unhealthy’ reading at 181, followed by Betong (MCAQM) at 180, Serian (MCAQM) at 179, and Kuching at 174.
The API in Sibu was 173, followed by Belaga (170), Sarikei (169), as well as Samarahan and Bintulu (168).
Mukah recorded an API of 162, while Samalaju and Miri both registered API readings of 158.
The API reading for both ILP Miri and Tebedu was 155, while Limbang recorded an API of 153.
Lawas recorded a reading of 128, followed by Kapit at 116 and Lundu at 105.
Bario was the only station recording a ‘Good’ API reading at 33.
Under the API classification, readings of 0 to 50 are considered ‘Good’, 51 to 100 ‘Moderate’, 101 to 200 ‘Unhealthy’, and 201 to 300 ‘Very Unhealthy’. — The Borneo Post

Title: Sarawak radio presenter dies at age 47 after collapsing at Kuching RTM office
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 23 — A radio presenter for RED FM at Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM) Sarawak, Azrani Azmi, 47, died after being found unconscious at his office at RTM Sarawak last night.
His younger sister, NurFarrah Hanna Azmi, said colleagues found him at about 8.40pm and rushed him to Sarawak General Hospital.
“As of this morning, the family is still awaiting the post-mortem results to determine the cause of death.
“He did not suffer from any critical illnesses, although he had high blood pressure,” she told Bernama.
His remains are expected to be buried at the Samariang Muslim Cemetery. — Bernama

Title: Tribunal orders former director of a Sabah hospital to apologise, pay RM10,000 over sexual harassment complaint
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 23 — A former Sabah hospital director has been ordered by the Tribunal for Anti-Sexual Harassment (TAGS) to pay RM10,000 in compensation to a woman who lodged a police report alleging sexual harassment against him.
His counsel Joan Goh (pic) said TAGS also ordered her client to apologise to the woman and pay the compensation via bank transfer within 30 days of the award dated Sept 18.
She said the apology must be sent to the woman via the TAGS email address, while two witnesses for the woman and five for the respondent testified during the hearing.
Goh said her client would challenge the Tribunal’s decision in the High Court through judicial review and seek a stay of the award pending determination of the challenge.
“The respondent maintains that the decision is legally unsustainable and raises serious issues warranting consideration by the High Court, including whether the Tribunal took into account irrelevant considerations and evidence in arriving at its findings, and whether the relevant statutory requirements for a finding of sexual harassment were properly considered and applied,” she said. — Daily Express

Title: Hajiji: Sabah can play bigger role in Malaysia-China ties
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 23 — Sabah is in a strategic position to become an important bridge in further strengthening cooperation between Malaysia and China, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said Sabah’s ties with China form an important part of the broader Malaysia-China cooperation, with relations between the two sides having been established for a long time through maritime trade routes.
“For centuries, maritime trade routes have connected coastal communities in Borneo with southern China as well as other areas in Southeast Asia.
“This relationship enabled the exchange of goods, ideas, culture, and societies, thereby creating bonds that remain meaningful to this day,” he said through a statement issued by the Chief Minister’s Department yesterday.
The statement added that Hajiji’s speech in conjunction with the 77th Anniversary Reception of the Founding of the People’s Republic of China at the Magellan Sutera Resort here was delivered by Sabah Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam.
Hajiji said that its strategic geographical location, economic potential, rich natural resources, and long-standing people-to-people relations enable Sabah to offer a strong platform for the engagement of Chinese enterprises, institutions, and communities.
“Trade and investment remain key pillars of Sabah-China relations. China is one of Sabah’s most important trading partners, with cooperation encompassing commodities, agriculture, fisheries, manufactured products, tourism, and services.
“Chinese companies operating in Sabah have contributed to economic development, job creation, infrastructure development, and stronger business connections,” he said.
He added that Sabah also offers vast investment opportunities to Chinese investors in the tourism, renewable energy, agriculture, fisheries, logistics, digital services, and blue economy sectors.
According to him, there is also ample room for both sides to share expertise in the fields of agriculture, marine conservation, clean energy, smart agriculture, and aquaculture.
Hajiji said cooperation in the tourism sector can also be further enhanced through stronger air connectivity, expanded digital marketing, and the development of ecotourism, cultural tourism, and adventure tourism.
Besides economic cooperation, he said there is great potential to expand collaboration in education and culture, including through university partnerships, student exchanges, language programmes, research, scholarships, as well as science and technology fields.
He added that Sabah remains committed to supporting strong and constructive relations between Malaysia and China while pursuing the state’s priorities under the Sabah Maju Jaya 2.0 development agenda.
“Sabah is ready and aspires to be an important platform for Malaysia-China cooperation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Thai imam’s wife finds paint splashed on car after prayers in Tumpat, Kelantan police on the case
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 23 — Police have confirmed receiving a report of an act of mischief on a car belonging to the wife of a Thai imam at the Kok Majid Jetty area in Tumpat Monday.
Tumpat police chief ACP Mohd Khairi Shafie said the 30-year-old imam had parked the white Honda City near the jetty at 7.10pm before heading to Masjid Pulau Beluru for Isyak prayers.
“After completing his prayers and returning to the location at 9.36pm, the complainant discovered paint marks on the vehicle,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Mohd Khairi said the imam had earlier received a screenshot from a friend, alleging he was threatened for tipping off the authorities about undocumented migrant smuggling in the Tumpat islands.
“The complainant, however, denied the allegation,” he said.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 427 of the Penal Code, including a possible link to the information the complainant received before the incident.
Anyone with information is urged to contact the Tumpat District Police Headquarters operations room at 09-7252482 or the nearest police station. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan exco overstepped its powers by suspending two top officials, says AGC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) has stated that the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council has no legal authority to suspend the duties of the state secretary (SUK) and state legal adviser.
In a statement yesterday, the AGC said appointment matters, including the suspension of duties for both positions, fall under the jurisdiction of the Public Services Commission and the Judicial and Legal Services Commission respectively, as stipulated under Article 37 of the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution 1959 (UUTKNS).
“On the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar’s Sept 22, 2026 media statement suspending the SUK and state legal adviser with immediate effect, this department is of the view that the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council has no legal authority to do so,” the AGC said.
The AGC added that the appointment of a new state legal adviser must comply with Article 37 of the UUTKNS, namely appointment by the Judicial and Legal Services Commission from among members of the Judicial and Legal Service.
Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today announced the immediate suspension of the duties of SUK Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal.
Ismail also announced that state financial officer Datuk Masri Razali would carry out the duties of the SUK until a new appointment is made by the Chief Secretary to the Government.
Meanwhile, advocate and solicitor Fahmi Adilah will carry out legal advisory duties until a new state legal adviser is appointed by the AGC. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: SUK is the abbreviation in Malay for Setiausaha Kerajaan Negeri while the initials UUTKNS stands fori Undang-Undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan.

Title: Landslide forces Cheras apartment residents out of their homes, underground water leak suspected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Residents of an apartment block in Bandar Damai Perdana, Cheras, were ordered to evacuate their homes last night following a landslide near the building, believed to have been caused by an underground water leak.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the on-site operations commander ordered residents near Block A of the apartment complex to immediately evacuate their homes as a precautionary measure.
He said the department received an emergency call regarding the incident at 9:03pm, and a team of five personnel with a fire engine from Bandar Tun Hussein Onn Fire and Rescue Station was deployed to the scene.
He added that the rescue team, arriving eight minutes later, found that a landslide involving a 4.57-metre-high slope had occurred.
“The distance the soil slid into the collapse area was approximately 0.91 metre,” he said in a statement last night.
Ashrul Riezal said observations revealed that water was still flowing in the area, though no further soil movement had been detected by the rescue team so far.
“Monitoring of the soil condition and water flow is actively being carried out to ensure safety at the scene,” he said.
He noted that there were no casualties or injuries resulting from the incident, and the Public Works Department has been informed for further action. — Bernama

Title: Anwar to meet 21 Chinese business leaders in Shanghai and Hangzhou as Malaysia courts fresh investment
Article:
SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to hold a roundtable business engagement and deliver a keynote address at the WorldSkills Conference 2026 here today.
Anwar will begin his programme with an engagement with about 21 Chinese captains of industry as part of the efforts to attract quality and impactful investments into Malaysia.
He will then attend the opening ceremony of the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 competition, to be officiated by Chinese Premier Li Qiang at the National Exhibition and Convention Centre.
Held from Sept 22 to 27, WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 is a major international platform showcasing excellence in technical and vocational skills.
In the 48th WorldSkills Competition, Malaysia is represented by 22 participants competing in 21 skill categories under the “Road to Gold” agenda, aimed at securing the country’s first gold medal at the prestigious global competition.
About 1,400 skilled young people from over 65 countries and regions are gathering in China’s largest city to compete across 64 skill categories.
In the afternoon, the Prime Minister and his delegation will travel by high-speed train to Hangzhou, the capital of Zhejiang province, for the second leg of the visit.
Upon arrival, Anwar is slated to hold one-on-one business meetings with tech giants AgiBot, Huawei and Alibaba Group as well as automotive company Geely and Chinese multinational technology and telecommunications equipment company ZTE Group.
Anwar will later attend a welcoming dinner hosted by Li.
The Prime Minister is also scheduled to launch a book titled “Rethinking Ourselves: Justice, Reform, and Ignorance in Postnormal Times”, which has been translated into Mandarin.
China remains Malaysia’s largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with total bilateral trade reaching US$113.82 billion (RM456.68 billion) for the period of January to August this year.
The Prime Minister arrived here on Tuesday for a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou. — Bernama

Title: Najib’s house arrest explained: 10 questions about pardons, prison powers and what happens next
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Malaysia does not have a specific house-arrest law. Yet the Prisons Department already has powers that can, under certain conditions, allow prisoners to remain outside prison while their sentences are still running.
That distinction has come into focus after former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak was granted a conditional pardon on September 18 allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International jail sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine and other conditions.
How does the arrangement work? What powers do the prison authorities already have, how is that different from a royal pardon, and what happens to Najib’s separate 1MDB sentence?
Here is a simplified guide based on the Prison Act 1995, the Prisons Regulations 2000, court judgments and news reports.
1. What were the terms of Najib’s September 18 conditional pardon?
Najib was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International jail sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and compliance with other conditions.
If Najib breaches any of the conditions, the conditional pardon will be revoked and he must immediately serve the remainder of his sentence in prison.
The pardon does not mean Najib was immediately transferred home.
As of September 21, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said Najib had yet to pay the RM50 million fine. Until that condition is fulfilled and the necessary process is completed, Najib remains in Kajang Prison.
2. Does Malaysia actually have a law specifically governing house arrest?
Short answer: No.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has said Malaysia does not yet have a specific law governing house arrest, although such legislation had previously been proposed for eligible remand detainees as part of efforts to reduce prison overcrowding.
The issue was also addressed by the High Court in December 2025, when then High Court judge Alice Loke ruled that an earlier order for Najib to serve his sentence under house arrest was invalid because it had not been deliberated or decided at the relevant Pardons Board meeting.
“In any event, I am of the view that a house arrest order is not capable of execution, there being no legal provision for such mechanism in Malaysia,” she said.
The judge also rejected Najib’s lawyers’ argument that Section 43 of the Prison Act could be used to implement that particular house-arrest order.
She said Section 43 gives prison authorities discretion over how long a prisoner may remain outside prison, whereas the disputed order specified how long Najib was to remain outside prison and restricted the authorities’ discretion to recall him to prison.
The judge nevertheless indicated that Najib could separately apply to the Prisons Department for release under Section 43.
3. So what power does the Prisons Department already have?
Under Section 43 of the Prison Act, the Commissioner General of Prisons may release a prisoner on licence and impose conditions on that release.
The release may be granted “at any time”.
If a prisoner fails to comply with any of the conditions imposed, they can face a maximum fine of RM2,000, a maximum jail term of two years, or both.
The Commissioner General may also modify or cancel the conditions of the licence, recall the prisoner to prison and subsequently release the prisoner on licence again.
In other words, release on licence provides a legal mechanism for a prisoner to remain outside prison while the original jail sentence is still running.
4. Could release on licence mean serving time at home?
Yes, potentially.
Under Regulation 111 of the Prisons Regulations 2000, the Commissioner General may release on licence a prisoner who has served at least four years of their sentence and impose conditions on that release.
That could potentially allow a prisoner to spend part of their sentence at home, if the Commissioner General specifies that as the place where they are required to remain.
The regulations do not spell out in detail other aspects of a prisoner’s life while released on licence, such as whether they may live with family members, receive visitors or communicate freely with people outside.
By comparison, the regulations contain detailed rules governing prisoners who remain in prison, including communication with relatives and friends, the frequency and duration of visits and the number of visitors permitted at one time.
Attorney General Mohd Dusuki said the Prisons Department is expected to issue standard operating procedures for Najib’s house-arrest arrangement, including rules covering visits, security and the monitoring of his movements.
Screenshot of part of a Release on Licence form (Schedule 2 of the Prisons Regulations 2000).
5. Has Section 43 been used before?
During a High Court hearing on November 24, 2025, Najib’s lawyer Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah claimed that Section 43 and Regulation 111 had previously been used to allow prisoners to spend periods of their sentences outside prison.
Shafee claimed the provisions had been used to allow Tun H.S. Lee’s grandson, Kenneth Lee Fook Mun — whose death sentence had been commuted to life imprisonment following a pardon — to serve the remainder of his jail term at home because his “aged father” was living there alone.
Shafee also argued before judge Alice Loke that Section 43 had been used to temporarily release a prisoner for a week to spend Hari Raya with his family, citing a June 4, 2019 news report titled “Kajang prison inmate gets to spend Raya at home with family”.
These were arguments put forward by Najib’s lawyer during the proceedings.
6. Who granted Najib the conditional pardon?
Short answer: The Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, granted the conditional pardon following the 64th meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya on September 18.
Under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, the Agong has the power to grant pardons for offences committed in the Federal Territories.
The Agong presides over meetings of the Federal Territories Pardons Board and exercises his pardoning power in accordance with the constitutional process involving the board.
Before the board gives its advice, it is required to consider the Attorney General’s written opinion on the matter.
Based on news reports, the Federal Territories Pardons Board currently includes Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh and former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain.
The announcement of Najib’s conditional pardon came from the Prime Minister’s Department’s Legal Affairs Division, or BHEUU, which serves as the Pardons Board’s secretariat.
7. What happened with Najib’s first SRC pardon and the earlier house-arrest order?
Najib has been in prison since August 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction in the SRC International case.
His original sentence was 12 years’ jail and a RM210 million fine.
In January 2024, his jail term was reduced to six years and his fine to RM50 million following a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting.
The reduced sentence carried an official release date of August 23, 2028 if the RM50 million fine was paid, or August 23, 2029 if it remained unpaid.
A separate add-on or addendum order by the then Agong purportedly allowed Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
But in December 2025, the High Court ruled that the addendum was constitutionally invalid because it had not been deliberated or decided at the Pardons Board meeting.
“The addendum order was not deliberated nor decided in the 61st Pardons Board meeting. There was no compliance with Article 42, consequently it is not a valid order,” the judge said.
Najib initially appealed against the decision but withdrew his appeal in April 2026.
The September 18 conditional pardon is therefore a separate and later decision by the Pardons Board and the King.
8. Could Najib’s SRC jail term end earlier?
Under Regulation 43, prisoners can get a one-third remission or reduction of their jail sentence, with the aim of encouraging good behaviour.
There has, however, been no announcement that Najib has been granted remission or that his SRC sentence has been shortened further on this basis.
Under the terms of his earlier pardon, Najib’s release date was stated as August 23, 2028 if he pays the RM50 million fine, or August 23, 2029 if the fine remains unpaid.
His latest conditional pardon allows him to serve the remainder of that sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, provided the stipulated conditions are fulfilled.
9. What about Najib’s 1MDB conviction and jail sentence?
The pardons discussed above concern Najib’s SRC International conviction.
On December 26, 2025, the High Court found Najib guilty in the RM2 billion 1MDB case and sentenced him to 15 years in prison, with that sentence ordered to begin after he completes his SRC sentence.
Najib is appealing against his conviction and sentence in the 1MDB case, and the Court of Appeal has yet to hear the appeal.
There have been no reports so far that Najib has applied for or obtained a stay of the 1MDB prison sentence pending the outcome of his appeal.
10. What happens next?
For now, Najib remains in Kajang Prison.
His lawyers said on September 20 that his transfer to house arrest depends on the conditions attached to the conditional pardon being fulfilled and that, until the fine is paid, he will remain in prison.
The Attorney General confirmed the following day that the RM50 million fine had not yet been paid and said payment must be made at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Registrar’s Office.
The Prisons Department is also expected to issue SOPs governing the practical implementation of the house-arrest arrangement.
Once the required conditions are met, the process for moving Najib from Kajang Prison to house arrest can proceed.

Title: ‘Sometimes I make only RM5’: Traders struggle as Rantau Panjang’s once-bustling bazaar falls quiet
Article:
PASIR MAS, Sept 23 — There are days when dry food seller Sapinah Abdul Rahman, 66, earns only RM5 to RM10 in profit from her business at Bazar Siti Fatimah in Rantau Panjang.
However, the woman continues to open her stall as it is the only source of income she has left to make a living.
“This bazaar used to be very lively, packed with food stalls and people. Now, those days are just memories. There are not many customers, and sometimes I make only RM5 to RM10 in profit a day.
“It is hardly worth the time and effort, but we still have to make a living,” she told Bernama recently.
Rantau Panjang once enjoyed its heyday as a bustling town, drawing visitors and lined with rows of business premises. However, its economic hub has now become increasingly quiet, including Bazar Siti Fatimah.
The situation has prompted traders and residents to hope that the town’s development will be given attention in Budget 2027, not merely to attract more visitors, but also to ensure that traders continue to have opportunities to earn a living.
A Bernama check found Bazar Siti Fatimah to be quiet on weekdays, with some premises closed, while trading activity was also subdued.
Some parts of the area also appeared poorly maintained, with bird droppings and structures used by birds for nesting visible.
Trading activity at Bazar Siti Fatimah in Rantau Panjang remains subdued, with some stalls closed and traders struggling with dwindling customer numbers. — Bernama pic
Sapinah said the bazaar’s condition needed to be addressed comprehensively, including through improvements to facilities, the provision of new attractions and promotional efforts to attract more visitors.
“If there is development and new attractions, people will come. When people come, traders like us will also have opportunities to earn a living,” she said.
She also hoped that the local authority (PBT) would play a more active role in ensuring that the area remained clean, well-maintained and comfortable for traders and visitors.
“Don’t just collect the rent. We hope there will be efforts to develop this place. If this place is vibrant and more people come, traders can also do better business,” she said.
For clothing seller Kamarudin Jusoh, 60, the situation had also made him consider giving up his business, but his age and difficulty in finding other employment had led him to continue relying on the business.
He said that with shop rental of RM280 a month, his income was now barely enough to cover his daily needs.
Bazar Siti Fatimah in Rantau Panjang, once a bustling trading centre, has seen business slow sharply, with traders saying customer numbers have dwindled. — Bernama pic
“I’m old. I have tried looking for other work, but I’m not qualified. So, I can only continue with this business. The rent is RM280 a month, but there are no customers. I just live from hand to mouth,” he said.
Kamarudin hoped that the plight of petty traders at Bazar Siti Fatimah would receive the attention of the relevant authorities through more structured measures to revive economic activity in Rantau Panjang.
He said the redevelopment of the area would not only attract visitors, but also provide opportunities for small traders to continue earning a living.
“I sincerely hope that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim can help us. I hope the development of Rantau Panjang town will be mentioned in Budget 2027 and receive the prime minister’s attention.
“We hope that the town can be brought back to life so that small traders like us can continue to earn a living and the local economy can become vibrant again,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Melaka election ahead: Key players, shifting alliances and the possible implications for Putrajaya
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The last time Melaka went to the polls, voters masked up, kept their distance in queues at polling stations and regularly sanitised their hands.
Five years on, the Covid-19 restrictions are gone, but shifting political tides and fluid alliances are set to shape another closely watched state election.
Melaka, traditionally a Barisan Nasional (BN) stronghold, fell to Pakatan Harapan (PH) for the first time in 2018 before BN wrested the state back with a two-thirds majority in the 2021 state election.
BN won 21 seats in the 28-seat state assembly in 2021, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.
The assembly’s composition subsequently changed after Rembia assemblyman Datuk Muhammad Jailani Khamis left BN for PAS, reducing BN’s representation to 20 seats. Bemban assemblyman Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub was also expelled from Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia and became an Independent while remaining in the Opposition bloc.
Following the formation of the unity government at the federal level in 2022, the five PH assemblymen — four from DAP and one from Amanah — joined the BN-led Melaka administration in 2023.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh announced yesterday that the state assembly would be dissolved today after receiving the consent of Melaka Governor Tun Mohd Ali Rustam, paving the way for the state’s 16th election. The assembly’s term had been due to expire on December 27.
Key players and the big battles
The election will be a significant test of Ab Rauf’s leadership. A first-term assemblyman, he became chief minister in March 2023 after his predecessor Datuk Seri Sulaiman Md Ali stepped down.
Ab Rauf is widely expected to defend his Tanjung Bidara seat for a second term.
Another high-profile contender is Umno Youth chief and Merlimau assemblyman Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh.
Akmal, an outspoken critic of DAP, tendered his resignation from the state executive council in January amid tensions over Umno’s cooperation with DAP and the unity government, but Ab Rauf rejected his resignation in April.
On PH’s side, the state’s sole Amanah representative, Adly Zahari, would be among the coalition’s most senior figures contesting the Melaka polls if he defends his Bukit Katil seat.
Adly, a former Melaka chief minister and currently the deputy defence minister, initially remained seated with the government bloc after his four DAP colleagues moved to the Opposition benches in July.
Melaka PH subsequently confirmed that all five of its assemblymen would withdraw from the state administration after the coalition opposed amendments to the state constitution allowing the appointment of nominated assemblymen.
The amendment allows for the appointment of up to seven nominated assemblymen, a measure opposed by all five PH representatives.
Two-thirds unlikely without allies
Pacific Research Centre of Malaysia principal adviser Oh Ei Sun expects BN to retain Melaka by a simple majority but said it would require an alliance with PN to reach a two-thirds majority.
BN enters the election after returning to power in Negeri Sembilan through an electoral understanding with PN.
The results reflected BN’s willingness to tailor its electoral strategy to different political terrains.
In Johor, BN contested all 56 state seats without an electoral alliance and went on to form the state government on its own.
In Negeri Sembilan, however, BN and PN reached an electoral understanding aimed at avoiding contests against one another despite BN remaining part of the PH-led federal government.
Whether a similar arrangement will be replicated in Melaka remains unsettled.
BN has indicated that negotiations with potential partners would take place following the dissolution of the state assembly, while Melaka PH has also been in discussions with Bersatu over a possible “PH Plus” arrangement.
Political analyst Datuk Sivamurugan Pandian from Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) said a BN-PN arrangement could consolidate the Malay vote in Melaka, making it more difficult for PH to make significant gains.
PH has suffered consecutive setbacks in recent state elections, and Sivamurugan said rebuilding confidence among Malay voters and giving greater prominence to local issues would be crucial if the coalition hoped to reverse its fortunes.
“PH has to acknowledge that Johor and Negeri Sembilan were not isolated defeats but are signals of changing voter behaviour,” Sivamurugan said.
Both Sivamurugan and Oh, however, said even a commanding BN victory in Melaka would be unlikely to trigger an early general election.
“The general election is at most about a year away, not two or three years away.
“So, it [forcing a snap election] wouldn’t make much difference,” Oh said, adding that BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s relationship with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim would also make it less likely that the federal government would be brought down before the end of its term.

Title: Selangor Malay Reserve Land up 1,084.55 hectares since 2018, says Amirudin
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 22 — The total area of Malay Reserve Land in Selangor has increased by 1,084.55 hectares (2,680 acres) since 2018, said Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
In a statement today, Amirudin said the overall area under the state government’s administration had increased from 162,161.98 hectares (400,711 acres) to 163,246.54 hectares (403,391 acres).
“Since 2018, the total area of Malay Reserve Land in Selangor under this administration has increased by 1,084.55 hectares (2,680 acres) compared to the previous government,” he said, in response to questions raised regarding the status of Malay Reserve Land in Sabak Bernam.
Meanwhile, Amirudin said that 22.41 hectares (55.401 acres) of land in Tanjong Karang, Sabak Bernam, which was degazetted through a gazette published on Sept 3, 2026, had been allocated for the Sabak Bernam Development Area (SABDA).
He added that to balance local development with the interests of Malay Reserve Land, a separate 22.41-hectare plot of land in Hulu Selangor was concurrently undergoing the gazetting process as Malay Reserve Land.
Amirudin said SABDA was an initiative by the Selangor state government to develop the northern corridor of Selangor to enhance food security and tap into the agro-tourism potential along the state’s west coast.
“At the same time, it will also increase employment opportunities for locals,” he said.
Amirudin said the effort was spearheaded by the state government subsidiary, Menteri Besar Selangor (Incorporated) or MBI, and involved local communities such as fishermen, entrepreneurs and academics. — Bernama

Title: Just 40m long, new Mont Kiara road opens shortcut to Solaris and Segambut
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — A new road measuring just 40 metres has opened in Mont Kiara, creating a direct connection between Jalan Duta Kiara and Jalan Kiara 3 and giving motorists an alternative route towards Solaris Dutamas, Segambut and surrounding areas.
The RM3 million two-way link, fully funded by developer Bon Estates as part of its corporate social responsibility programme, is expected to reduce lengthy detours for residents in the densely developed neighbourhood, the
New Straits Times
reported.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said Jalan Duta Kiara had previously ended in a dead end, forcing motorists travelling between Bukit Pelangi and Solaris to take a longer route despite the two areas being close to one another.
“Before this road was constructed, those from Bukit Pelangi wanting to go to Solaris could not simply cross over despite the areas being so close.
“Everybody had to be stuck in the traffic. For residents here, they had to make a big round just to get home.
“With this connection, you can turn left or right, while traffic from the other side can come straight through,” she was quoted as saying after opening the road today.
Yeoh said the project followed discussions involving the developer, the Mont Kiara Residents’ Association and other local stakeholders over traffic and connectivity concerns in the area.
“I am very happy with the process of engagement with the stakeholders. This is how every development should be.
“You hear the feedback from the member of parliament, engage the local residents’ association and meet the needs of the local community,” she said.
According to the report, the new route would also provide another option for motorists travelling near a school along the existing road network.
Yeoh said Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) was also planning another road connection from Jalan Kiara 7 to the Sprint Highway via the Penchala Link, which would further expand access in Mont Kiara.
“Mont Kiara has about 50 condominiums. I cannot undo the development because it was already like that when I was elected.
“But over the last few years, we have worked very hard with private developers and DBKL to facilitate the opening of more roads and give people greater access,” she said.
Yeoh said congestion and limited road connectivity remained among the main concerns raised by residents, particularly those travelling between neighbouring residential and commercial areas.
There is currently no estimate of how many vehicles are expected to use the new connection, she added, noting that DBKL had to balance infrastructure spending across different parliamentary constituencies.

Title: KPWKM seeks higher Budget 2027 allowances for disabled workers and PDK staff, says Nancy
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 22 — The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) has proposed higher allowances for disabled workers and staff at Community Rehabilitation Centres (PDK) under Budget 2027, the minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said.
She said the ministry was committed to ensuring that persons with disabilities (PwD) and those involved in caregiving received appropriate support, particularly to improve their quality of life.
“Regarding the allowances for PDK trainers, we have proposed increasing them, but approval has not yet been given. We have to wait for the Budget announcement to know whether it will be approved.
“Most PDKs depend on external donations and support from elected representatives in their respective areas. That is why elected representatives often raise the matter and call for higher allowances to help the communities they serve,” she said.
She said this at a press conference after officiating the closing ceremony of the Able for Disable Programme and the presentation of certificates for the AEON Job Coach Introduction Course 2026 here today.
Nancy said ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027, her ministry also hoped its proposal to strengthen the care economy would be approved.
“We want it to become a successful programme for those in need, including PwD and those caring for PwD, so we hope the proposals we have made will receive approval,” she said.
In her speech at the event, Nancy urged all parties to move beyond simply employing PwD towards developing their talents and careers.
She said the private sector had a significant role to play given the abundance of employment opportunities available, and urged employers to assess the potential and contributions that PwD could offer.
“At the same time, I urge organisations to involve the PwD community itself in planning an inclusive work environment and employment system. The principle is simple: we should not assume what PwD need without listening to their own experiences.
“In KPWKM's accessibility agenda, the PwD community is also emphasised as users and partners who must be involved in evaluating the solutions developed, because the true measure of inclusivity is the experience of those who use the system,” she said. — Bernama

Title: MCMC ready to license e-commerce platforms once ministries set conditions, says deputy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Communications Ministry is waiting for the terms and conditions from the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) and the Finance Ministry (MoF) before licensing e-commerce platforms.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has the power under the existing legal framework to license the platforms, but the specific conditions must be decided by the relevant ministries.
“Yes, we actually had a discussion with the MOF together with KPDN. I think KPDN’s decision is to study how to regulate these e-commerce platforms. MCMC, or the Ministry of Communications, is involved because under the Malaysian legal framework, we have the power to actually license e-commerce platforms.
“However, we are waiting for instructions or feedback from MoF, (and) especially from KPDN, on the terms and conditions to be imposed,” she told reporters after attending the media launch of the Asean-China Cross Border E-Commerce Expo 2026 (CBE2026) at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre (KLCC) here today.
Teo said MCMC was ready to implement the licensing once the framework was in place to ensure a fair business environment.
She was responding to growing concerns among local retailers over the presence of a major China-based e-commerce platform known for its ultra-low-cost products.
“MCMC is ready anytime. We have engaged with the platform as well, but again, this is not just targeting it, but all e-commerce platforms. We want to level the playing field and make sure that Malaysian consumers are protected,” she said.
Meanwhile, when asked about DAP secretary-general and Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s offer to resign, Teo said the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) had decided that all its ministers and deputy ministers would remain in their respective positions.
She said their continued presence in the Cabinet was a strong testament to their unwavering support for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s leadership. — Bernama

Title: Magnitude 4.4 earthquake detected off Batu Pahat, tremors felt onshore
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Sept 22 — A magnitude 4.4 earthquake was detected off the coast of Batu Pahat at 4.55pm today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the earthquake struck at a depth of 10 kilometres, with its epicentre at 1.7 degrees north and 102.7 degrees east, about 27 kilometres southwest of Batu Pahat.
Tremors were felt in Batu Pahat and surrounding areas, MetMalaysia said, adding that it would continue to monitor the situation. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak’s next legislative assembly sitting will be the last of current term, says state Speaker
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 22 — The coming Sarawak Legislative Assembly (DUN) will be the last one for this term, said Speaker Tan Sri Datuk Amar Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar.
However, he said the dates of the coming DUN sitting have not been announced yet.
“As usual, I will call a press conference for the DUN,” he told reporters after the “Kenegaraan Aku Kasih Malaysia: Pimpinan Belia Negeri Sarawak” seminar here.
“As you all know, the date has been disclosed. Not from the secretary or from me, but from the Opposition — they said this is the date and so forth. So, I will call a press conference before the DUN,” said Asfia.
On September 10, The Borneo Post sighted a Sarawak Government Gazette stating that, pursuant to Standing Order 8(2) of the Standing Orders of the DUN Sarawak, the premier of Sarawak had determined that the sitting would be held from October 12 to 21, 2026.
The notification was dated September 10 and signed by the Secretary of the DUN Sarawak.
Asked whether any Bills, particularly important ones, would be tabled during the sitting, Asfia said his office had yet to receive any Bills from the state government.
“My office has not received any Bill from the government. Not yet,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Anwar arrives in Shanghai for three-day working visit
Article:
SHANGHAI, Sept 22 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived here on Tuesday for a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, China, aimed at strengthening Malaysia-China ties, boosting trade and expanding cooperation in emerging technologies.
The aircraft carrying Anwar and his delegation landed at Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport at 5.10pm local time (5.10pm Malaysian time).
He was welcomed by Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad and Consul General of Malaysia in Shanghai Abdullah Ma’amor Ibrahim.
Also present were Shanghai Vice-Mayor of Shanghai Wang Huajie, China’s Ambassador to Malaysia Ouyang Yujing, and Su Lin, a member of the Party Leadership Group of the Shanghai Municipal Foreign Affairs Office.
The visit, at the invitation of the Chinese government, is Anwar’s fourth visit to China since he became the prime minister in 2022.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, is accompanied by Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry, Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
The highlight of the visit will be Anwar’s high-level meeting with the Chinese Premier Li Qiang in Hangzhou, the capital city of Zhejiang province, on Thursday.
In Shanghai, the prime minister is scheduled to attend the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 at the National Exhibition and Convention Centre (NECC), where he will deliver a keynote address at the plenary session of the WorldSkills Conference 2026 on Wednesday.
He will also attend the Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo in the eastern Chinese city of Hangzhou, where Malaysia and Hungary are participating as Guest Countries of Honour.
The prime minister is also scheduled to deliver a keynote address at the expo, one of China’s major digital economy platforms, which will highlight artificial intelligence (AI) and global cooperation
During the visit, Anwar is also expected to engage Chinese industry leaders in a roundtable session and one-on-one meetings with key industry and tech giants to drive foreign direct investment into Malaysia.
China has remained Malaysia’s largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with total bilateral trade reaching USD113.82 billion (RM456.68 billion) between January and August this year. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan govt suspends state secretary, legal adviser amid royal row
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Negeri Sembilan government today suspended the state secretary and state legal adviser with immediate effect amid the ongoing dispute involving the state’s royal institution.
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the decision was made unanimously at a special meeting of the State Executive Council (MMKN) today.
The two officials are State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and State Legal Adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal.
In a statement, Ismail said State Financial Officer Datuk Masri Razali would assume the duties of the state secretary until a new state secretary is appointed by the Chief Secretary to the Government.
He said legal advisory duties would meanwhile be carried out by lawyer Fahmi Adilah until a new state legal adviser is appointed by the Attorney-General’s Chambers.
“The suspension notice for the Negeri Sembilan State Secretary will be conveyed to the Chief Secretary to the Government and the Public Service Department.
“Meanwhile, the suspension notice for the Negeri Sembilan State Legal Adviser will be conveyed to the Attorney-General’s Chambers,” he said.
Ismail also maintained that all positions held by members of the State Executive Council (MMKN) remained valid and lawful.
“I also confirm that all positions of members of the State Executive Council (MMKN) remain intact and valid,” he said.
The development comes amid an escalating dispute involving the position of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
On Sunday, Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of all 10 state executive councillors, saying they had breached their oaths of office.
Ismail subsequently said he had not advised or been consulted on the revocation and maintained that the existing EXCO line-up remained valid.
Ismail said the state administration would continue to function as usual and that its responsibilities towards the people would continue to be carried out to the best of its ability.

Title: Melaka to keep running as usual as state assembly heads for dissolution
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 22 — Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has given assurance that the Melaka state government’s affairs will continue to run as usual even though the Melaka State Legislative Assembly (DUN) is dissolved effective tomorrow.
He said the state administration, public service delivery, public welfare affairs, security and the government’s daily services will continue to operate as usual.
“Following this dissolution, the state government will carry out its responsibilities in the capacity of a caretaker government until a new state government is formed after the election process.
“Throughout this period, our priority is to ensure that the state administration remains orderly, services to the people are uninterrupted, and the people’s interests continue to be safeguarded,” he said.
Ab Rauf said this at a press conference when announcing the dissolution date of the Melaka DUN, which will take effect tomorrow, at the Seri Negeri Auditorium here today.
He said all departments, state government agencies and local authorities will continue to carry out their respective duties and responsibilities professionally based on prevailing laws, regulations and governance.
“The state will continue to be well-administered, services to the people will continue to run, and the interests of the people will remain our priority,” he said.
Asked whether he would retain existing candidates from Barisan Nasional (BN) and cooperation partners from other parties to participate in this democratic arena, Ab Rauf said it would be announced later.
“I don’t want to answer that now, let’s wait. I can’t reveal that because we will take many factors into account. So I can’t announce today — the day I dissolve [the assembly] — who the candidates will be... that wouldn’t be fair to me.
“I will announce that later when we have finalised all discussions,” he said.
The 15th Melaka State Election (PRN) was held on Nov 20, 2021, after four state assemblymen (Adun) supporting the government withdrew their support for the leadership of former Chief Minister Datuk Seri Sulaiman Md Ali on Oct 4, 2021.
The four assemblymen were former Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Idris Haron (BN-Sungai Udang), Datuk Nor Azman Hassan (BN-Pantai Kundor), Datuk Noor Effandi Ahmad (Bersatu-Telok Mas) and Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee (Independent-Pengkalan Batu).
In that state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 seats — with UMNO securing 18 seats, MCA two and MIC one — thereby forming the state government with a more than two-thirds majority.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) won five seats through DAP with four seats and Amanah one, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) won two seats.
However, political dynamics led to seat changes after Rembia assemblyman from BN, Datuk Muhammad Jailani Khamis, joined PAS, while Bemban assemblyman from Bersatu, Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub, was expelled from the party and became an independent assemblyman while remaining in the opposition bloc.
This caused BN to lose one seat but it still maintained a majority in the DUN with 20 seats, thus not affecting the state government’s administration.
The term of the Melaka DUN was set to end on Dec 27. — Bernama

Title: Tasik Bera enforcement: Five arrested, investigation papers to be referred to DPP
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 22 — Police have received 24 reports in connection with operations at the Tasik Bera Conservation Forest Reserve in Bera as of yesterday.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the reports were lodged by members of the Orang Asli community and enforcement personnel.
“The operation is ongoing, and we urge the public to cooperate with enforcement personnel in carrying out their duties,” he told reporters after attending the handover-of-duties ceremony for the Pahang Police Management Department chief at the Pahang Police Contingent Headquarters here today.
Azry Akmar said the investigation papers on five individuals arrested on Sept 15 for allegedly obstructing enforcement officers during the operation would be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor soon.
Police had earlier arrested four women and a man, aged between their 30s and 60s, to assist in investigations under Section 186 of the Penal Code.
In an unrelated development, Azry Akmar said police had opened two investigation papers following a recent altercation at a religious school in Bukit Ibam, Rompin.
He said the first case involved two male victims, both aged 14, and five suspects who were Form Four and Form Five students.
“The second case involved another 14-year-old male victim and six suspects. Further investigations found that four of the suspects were also involved in the first case,” he said, adding that the investigation was being conducted under Section 147 of the Penal Code.
Azry Akmar said both investigation papers would be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor today for further instructions.
At the event, Azry Akmar witnessed the handover of duties between outgoing Pahang Police Management Department chief SAC Mohd Fakhrurazie Che Sulaiman and his successor, Supt Afandi Hussin.
Mohd Fakhrurazie has been transferred to Bukit Aman to head the Anti-Money Laundering Crime Investigation Unit under the Inspector-General of Police Secretariat.  — Bernama

Title: PKR’s Hassan Karim urges Anwar to retain Anthony Loke ahead of major transport projects
Article:
PASIR GUDANG, Sept 22 — Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim has called on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to persuade Anthony Loke to remain as transport minister to ensure the completion of several key infrastructure projects, including those in Johor.
The PKR lawmaker expressed concern that Loke’s resignation could jeopardise ongoing projects, including those in Johor.
“These include projects such as the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS), the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL), the proposed Pasir Gudang railway line, and the rapid transit system, which have yet to be fully implemented.
“However, Anwar should first hear out Loke’s reasons before deciding to accept his offer to resign.
“I hope the prime minister takes my view into consideration and persuades Loke to stay. We are drawing closer to the general election and Loke is an asset to the government and the ruling Pakatan Harapan (PH) coalition,” he told reporters after a dialogue session between transport operators and businesspeople, with officials from the Johor chapter of the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) and the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN) at Lepak Corner here today.
Hassan said his remarks were based on precedents where national leaders had been known to reject the resignation of members of their administration, including during the federal government of the first prime minister, Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj.
“This demonstrates that a resignation need not necessarily be accepted, particularly when the services of a minister or administration member are still deemed essential,” he said, citing the recent example of Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh rejecting the resignation of Datuk Muhamad Akmal Saleh as a state executive councillor.
On a personal level, Hassan described Loke’s decision to offer his resignation following the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak as a responsible move.
However, the social activist noted that the final decision on whether Loke should leave the Cabinet rests with the prime minister.
“Anwar gave his assurance and has indicated he would listen to the outgoing transport minister’s reasons before deciding,” he said.

Title: Melaka heads for polls as CM Rauf Yusoh confirms assembly set for dissolution tomorrow
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 22 — The Melaka State Legislative Assembly will be dissolved tomorrow to pave the way for the 16th state election.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh announced the matter at a press conference at the Seri Negeri Complex here today.
He said the dissolution had received the consent of Melaka Governor Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
“I would like to take this opportunity to express my deepest appreciation to the Governor of Melaka for his consent and wisdom in carrying out his functions as provided for under the law,” he said.
Ab Rauf said State Assembly Speaker Datuk Ibrahim Durum had also submitted the notice of dissolution to the Election Commission (EC).
The last Melaka state election was held on Nov 20, 2021, after four assemblymen withdrew their support for then Chief Minister Datuk Seri Sulaiman Md Ali, causing the state government to collapse.
They were former Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Idris Haron (BN-Sungai Udang), Datuk Nor Azman Hassan (BN-Pantai Kundor), Datuk Noor Effandi Ahmad (Bersatu-Telok Mas) and independent Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee (Pengkalan Batu).
Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats in the election, securing a more than two-thirds majority to form the state government.
Of the 21 seats, Umno won 18, MCA two and MIC one.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five seats, four of which through DAP and one through Amanah, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) won two.
The composition of the assembly subsequently changed after Rembia assemblyman Datuk Muhammad Jailani Khamis left BN for PAS, while Bemban assemblyman Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub was expelled from Bersatu and became an independent while remaining in the opposition bloc.
The changes reduced BN’s representation to 20 seats, but it retained a comfortable majority in the 28-seat assembly and continued to govern the state.
The current assembly’s term had been due to expire on Dec 27. — Bernama

Title: Three actors out on bail as police hunt uploader of viral Rukun Negara clip from 2018
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Bukit Aman have released three local actors on police bail after questioning them over a viral video of a 2018 theatre performance allegedly mocking the Rukun Negara, while investigators hunt for the person who re-uploaded the footage.
Federal Criminal Investigation Department irector Datuk M. Kumar said the performers, a man and two women aged 28, 29 and 47 respectively, were picked up in Selangor and Johor last Saturday.
“The three have since been released on police bail after their statements were recorded, and checks found no content from the performance on their mobile phones or other devices.
“We recorded their statements and released them on police bail because they cooperated and we had completed checks on their devices. Nothing was found, so there was no justification to remand them,” he told a press conference at the federal police headquarters here.
Kumar said police had identified five actors featured in the clip, adding that one has since diedf and the other is believed to currently be in the United Kingdom based on immigration records.
He said investigators are now tracing the person who uploaded the eight-year-old footage online, including through relevant Internet Protocol addresses.
“Someone has now circulated what happened in 2018 and we are tracking down the person who uploaded the video,” he said.
The performance was staged behind closed doors at a performing arts centre in Penang in 2018 as part of a competition involving several groups.
The performing arts centre has since closed, Kumar said.
He added that investigations showed the performance director is a UK national who has since left Malaysia.
The case is being investigated under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. — Bernama

Title: No drug arrests for a week? Kelantan police chief says two station heads get reprimand letters
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 22 — Two police station chiefs (OCSs) in Kelantan have received reprimand letters after they failed to record any drug-related arrests for a week, said state police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat.
He said further action might be taken if the OCSs did not improve their performance.
He said the state police headquarters is monitoring seven police stations with regard to enforcement against drug abuse and trafficking.
“If a particular station has no arrests at all for a week, I will ensure that a team from the Contingent Police Headquarters goes to the area.
“If the special task force from the IPK manages to make an arrest, the OCS concerned will be reprimanded,” he told a press conference after the Kelantan contingent police monthly assembly here today.
Mohd Yusoff said the performance of each police station is monitored weekly and presented at meetings with the head of the Narcotics Department.
He said OCSs who receive reprimand letters must ensure that their performance meets the key performance indicators again the following week.
Mohd Yusoff said a post-mortem would be conducted on Oct 15 following a three-month pilot period to identify the reasons certain police stations failed to meet the stipulated KPIs. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: OCS is short for Officer-in-Charge of Station.

Title: Melaka heads for polls? CM Ab Rauf set to make big announcement today
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 22 — Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh is expected to announce the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly at 2pm today, paving the way for the 16th state election.
The announcement is expected to be made at Kompleks Seri Negeri in Ayer Keroh.
Speculation over an imminent dissolution intensified after the state executive council meeting, usually held on Wednesdays, was brought forward by a day.
Ab Rauf is understood to have chaired the meeting at noon today.
The Chief Minister’s Office has also invited members of the media to a press conference scheduled for 2pm.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats contested, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.
The current state assembly’s term is due to expire on Dec 27. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s research has potential, now it needs to leave the lab, says higher education minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Malaysia’s research and innovation ecosystem has recorded more than 500 matched patents valued at over RM2 billion through the Malaysian R&D Commercialisation Portal, involving more than 120 active missions, showing that the country does not lack ideas or talent.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the milestone demonstrated Malaysia’s immense capacity for innovation, provided the gap between academic research and commercial market demands could be bridged effectively.
“Malaysia had many good researchers, ideas and promising innovations, but too many of them remained at the university level.
“For the first time, we are creating a dedicated platform for university researchers to bring their ideas directly to industry, investors and potential partners,” he said during the opening ceremony of the University Research and Innovation Investment Summit 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here today.
Meanwhile, Zambry urged local industry players to look inside Malaysian universities for technological solutions before turning to foreign providers.
He said while local institutions possess extensive talent, facilities and intellectual property, a lack of confidence often leads businesses to seek solutions outside the country.
“Research cannot end with a publication. Innovation cannot end with a patent. A prototype cannot remain in the laboratory. A discovery must become a solution. A prototype must become a product. And an idea must become an opportunity,” he said.
Zambry also called on investors to view university researchers not only as academics, but also as innovators, entrepreneurs and potential business partners.
Over the three-day summit, URIIS 2026 will cover at least nine strategic sectors, including food security, healthcare, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, green technology, mobility, defence and biodiversity. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: Neither MB Ismail Lasim nor I was summoned by Negeri Sembilan Ruler for an audience
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said neither he nor Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was summoned for an audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Negeri Sembilan here yesterday.
“No. Neither the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar nor I was ever summoned for an audience. We only learnt about it through the media,” he said when asked at a press conference after officiating the University Research and Innovation Investment Summit 2026 here today.
He said the ongoing dispute in Negeri Sembilan should be resolved properly, with due regard for both legal interpretations and the state’s institutions.
“In my view, this is not merely a question of legal interpretation and powers. The institutions and establishment in Negeri Sembilan must also be respected,” he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had an audience with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Negeri Sembilan in the capital yesterday, with the meeting lasting nearly an hour.
The audience followed Tuanku Muhriz’s decision to revoke the appointments of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council members with immediate effect, after finding that they had breached their oaths of office.
Ismail, however, has disputed the validity of the move, arguing that the dismissal or termination of an executive councillor without the advice or request of the Menteri Besar was legally flawed, unconstitutional and had no legal effect. — Bernama

Title: Finance pros cannot escape geopolitics in a changing world, says deputy finance minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Finance professionals must adapt to a rapidly changing global landscape shaped by geopolitical shifts, climate and sustainability challenges, artificial intelligence (AI) and growing concerns over trust.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the transformation of the global environment in recent years had created new challenges for businesses and finance professionals, requiring them to rethink how financial systems and structures are designed.
“If you are the ‘architect’ of a financial structure, you cannot run away from geopolitics. This is the time for accountants to equip themselves with geopolitical and geoeconomics knowledge to deal with the challenges to come,” he said in his keynote address at the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants Leadership Exchange Forum 2026.
Liew said the years ahead would be different from the period preceding 2020, with the Covid-19 pandemic and subsequent geopolitical conflicts transforming the global landscape.
As such, he emphasised the need for financial professionals to understand geopolitical developments worldwide, particularly as businesses face growing risks to investment, technology and supply chains.
He said supply chain resilience was one of the key issues, noting that for a long time, businesses had assumed goods would move automatically by container ships without having to consider their sources or the need for alternative sources of raw materials and what to do in the event of supply chain disruptions.
“I think these are the questions that those in the financial systems will have to ask,” said Liew.
On climate and sustainability, he said these are issues that accountants can no longer avoid, adding that the profession needs to consider ways to measure and manage them.
At the same time, he noted that accountants and businesses would need to adapt and transform their practices to maximise the benefits that AI has to offer.
The Leadership Exchange Forum, themed “Finance as Architect: Aligning Policy, Practice and Technology in the Age of AI”, brings together policymakers, finance leaders, technology experts and industry practitioners to examine how AI and data are reshaping the finance function and its role in driving business growth.
The forum will examine how finance professionals can bridge the gap between technology and human expertise while maintaining professional judgement, ethics and trust. — Bernama
